title: $μ$SR measurements of 3D Ising ferromagnetism in bulk Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$ crystals
authors: M. N. Wilson, J. Huang, T. J. Hicken, D. A. Mayoh, B. M. Huddart, G. Balakrishnan, T. Lancaster
abstract: Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$ is a quasi-two-dimensional itinerant ferromagnet with a van-der-Waals layered structure that exhibits substantial magnetic anisotropy. In bulk samples, this material becomes magnetically ordered below 220~K, while in thin samples, the gate-tunability of the ferromagnetic moment has attracted significant interest. Alongside high-temperature ferromagnetism, a low-temperature magnetic state occurs whose nature has not been conclusively identified, with some studies suggesting a transition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism with temperature. Here we present magnetometry and $μ$SR data that demonstrate that Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$ exhibits three-dimenional Ising-like ferromagnetism over the entire temperature range between $T_{C}=220$~K and 2~K. The feature at 170~K that has previously been proposed to be a transition to antiferromagnetism is instead likely to represent a domain-freezing transition.
summary: This work uses $\mu$SR and magnetometry on $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ to investigate its magnetic phase transitions. The authors argue that the material remains a 3D Ising ferromagnet down to 2 K, refuting previous claims of an antiferromagnetic transition at 170 K. The observed feature is instead attributed to domain-freezing dynamics.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve the debate regarding the magnetic state evolution in the itinerant ferromagnet $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$, specifically whether a transition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism occurs at low temperatures.
main_result: The measurements demonstrate that $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$ exhibits 3D Ising-like ferromagnetism across the entire temperature range studied, and the feature previously thought to be an antiferromagnetic transition is reinterpreted as a domain-freezing transition.
method: The research combines magnetometry (ZFC/FCC) with muon-spin relaxation ($\mu$SR) measurements performed in zero applied field, supplemented by DFT calculations for muon stopping sites.
model_or_system: The physical system is the layered van der Waals ferromagnet $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2$. The analysis compares experimental $\mu$SR data against theoretical simulations for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic magnetic structures.
key_observables: Muon polarization relaxation rates (NSR and SR modes), magnetization vs. temperature ($dM/dT$), and the temperature dependence of the internal magnetic field $B(T)$.
important_parameters: Curie temperature ($T_C \approx 220	ext{ K}$), the temperature of interest ($170	ext{ K}$), and the magnetic anisotropy inherent to the layered structure.
main_assumptions: The $\mu$SR measurement probes the bulk material ($\sim 200\ \mu	ext{m}$ depth), and the analysis relies on fitting the temperature dependence of the internal field to critical power laws.
figures_summary: Figures show magnetization curves indicating transitions at 170 K and 220 K. $\mu$SR data illustrate the relaxation behavior in both polarization modes at different temperatures, which are compared against simulations for competing magnetic states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents magnetometry and $\mu$SR data to challenge the assumption of an AF transition at 170 K. It uses detailed analysis of the temperature dependence of the internal field and compares results against theoretical models for both FM and AFM states to conclude the persistence of 3D Ising ferromagnetism.
why_interesting: The use of $\mu$SR to probe local magnetic fields and distinguish between competing magnetic ground states (FM vs. AFM) in a highly anisotropic, itinerant magnet is relevant to understanding magnetic ordering in low-dimensional quantum materials.
